items.title: Proudly Human Promises to Certify AI-Free Books
items.excerpt: Australian startup Proudly Human, founded by former chief scientist Alan Finkel, joins a growing field of services certifying books as written without AI assistance; Finkel says two of the Big Five are in talks.

items.title: 11 Books for Understanding the AI Debate
items.excerpt: As Anthropic heads toward an IPO and data centers become a political issue, PW rounds up 11 books on AI safety, risk and regulation for readers following the debate.

items.title: AAP Calls on Meta to Drop 'Onerous' Terms of Service
items.excerpt: The Association of American Publishers called Meta's new commercial terms, which would let it crawl business websites for AI training with no opt-out short of leaving its platforms, 'an appalling landgrab of unprecedented proportion.'

items.title: 'Does Meta think we can't read?' Meta abandons sketchy commercial terms update
items.excerpt: After backlash from publishers and businesses, Meta says it won't force Facebook page owners to allow AI training on linked content, pausing the commercial terms update.

items.title: Editor's letter: Can AI predict the Booker winner? Not likely
items.excerpt: The Bookseller's editor asked AI to predict the Booker Prize winner; 'believe the hype around AI if you must, but when asked to predict the future its limitations were plain to see.'

items.title: Copyright Infringement Lawsuit Against OpenAI Draws More than 50 Amicus Briefs
items.excerpt: More than 50 amicus briefs filed in the consolidated Authors Guild v. OpenAI case map the fault lines over AI training on books, pirated sources and infringing outputs ahead of summary judgment.

items.title: From AI Adoption to AI Practice: Building Governed AI in Scholarly Publishing
items.excerpt: Integra's Gregory Simmons and Ashutosh Ghildiyal lay out how publishers can deploy AI across editorial, integrity and marketing teams while keeping control of confidential manuscripts and accountability.

items.title: What AI Can't Learn About Peer Review... Because Nobody Can Explain It
items.excerpt: Taylor & Francis's Victoria Corless argues that generative AI can summarize manuscripts and check references, but automating peer review risks losing tacit editorial expertise nobody has documented.

items.title: How AI Is Changing the Way We Read, Learn, and Organize Information
items.excerpt: E-readers and reading apps increasingly let readers query, summarize and get explanations of texts with AI, which helps students and researchers but raises questions about deep reading.

items.title: 300 Authors File Individual Copyright Claims against Meta
items.excerpt: Some 300 authors filed individual copyright claims against Meta over LLM training on shadow-library books, each seeking $150,000 statutory damages per title, with 1,000 more claims expected.

items.title: Sharjah Translation Award Debate Highlights Limits Of AI In Literary Translation
items.excerpt: Translators, academics and publishers at the Sharjah Translation Award seminar at SIBF 2026 said AI can speed translation and research but cannot replace human judgment in literary work.

items.title: SIBF 2026: Does AI really pose a threat to writing? Booker winner Daisy Rockwell weighs in
items.excerpt: The Bookseller's editor asked AI to predict the Booker Prize winner; 'believe the hype around AI if you must, but when asked to predict the future its limitations were plain to see.'

items.title: AI errors, inflated prices: Tamil Nadu govt orders probe into Periyar library books
items.excerpt: Tamil Nadu ordered a probe after writer Perumal Murugan flagged suspected AI-generated books, phantom authors and factual errors among titles bought for the new Periyar Arivulagam library in Coimbatore.

items.title: Project Hail Mary Author Says He 'Might Be Among the Last Generation of Fully Human Writers'
items.excerpt: Andy Weir compares AI to hammers, forklifts and race cars and says he may be among the last generation of fully human writers.

items.title: What AI can lose when it makes Holocaust writings easier to read
items.excerpt: A Tel Aviv University study in AI & Society ran three Holocaust writings through AI enhancement, handwriting recognition, correction and translation, finding gains in access but losses in material evidence.

items.title: The founder of DOU and Djinni built his own AI-powered e-reader with Claude
items.excerpt: Max Ishchenko, founder of DOU and Djinni, vibe-coded his own reading service with built-in AI explanations and translations after being disappointed with standard e-readers.

items.title: University libraries are being swarmed by AI bots, putting public access at risk
items.excerpt: Academic libraries are fighting swarms of AI data-scraping bots that slow or crash digital collections meant for students, researchers and the public.

items.title: 내 독서 취향은 무슨 빵?…영풍문고, AI 도서 추천 '책빵집' 출시
items.excerpt: 영풍문고가 온라인 이용 기록과 전국 매장 판매 데이터를 함께 분석해 8가지 '빵' 독서 유형별로 책을 추천하는 AI 서비스 'AI 책빵집'을 내놨다.

items.title: AI가 소설 쓰고 독자가 다음 화 바꾼다…문체부 R&D 웹소설, 일본 진출
items.excerpt: AI 콘텐츠 스타트업 모사재인이 문체부·콘진원 R&D로 다중 AI 에이전트 웹소설 플랫폼 '아이로쿠'를 일본에 출시했다. 이용자가 캐릭터·세계관·태그를 고르면 AI가 한 화씩 소설을 쓴다.

items.title: 충남도교육청, AI 문해력 플랫폼 '온글' 도서 확대…출판사 참여 독려
items.excerpt: 충남교육청이 파주에서 출판사 100여 곳을 대상으로 AI 기반 문해력 플랫폼 '온글' 공개회를 열고, 독서 수준 진단·도서 추천·AI 글쓰기 피드백에 쓸 도서 등록을 요청했다.

items.title: AI와 출판산업, '정당한 거래 시장' 열리면 성장 동반자 될 수 있어
items.excerpt: 프랑크푸르트 호소문과 한국 출판계 호소문 이후, 바츠 대 앤트로픽 판결의 공정이용 판단을 짚으며 AI 학습용 도서의 정당한 거래 시장이 필요하다고 주장하는 칼럼.

items.title: [문소영의 직격인터뷰] "미국 AI 기업의 국내 도서 대량 매집, 구한말을 보는 듯"
items.excerpt: 지식재산권법 권위자 정상조 교수가 앤트로픽의 한국 도서 41만 권 매집 사태를 두고 국내 AI 학습 데이터 확보와 저작권 제도 전면 재설계를 주장했다.

items.title: [신간] 『창작자의 프롬프트 노트』
items.excerpt: GPT와 클로드에서 SF·로맨스·스릴러·역사판타지를 세 가지 지시 수준으로 교차한 32번의 서사 실험을 바탕으로 AI 시대 창작법을 다룬 신간.

items.title: Grok Says Its AI-Generated Version of 'The Odyssey' Is 'Not Historically Accurate'
items.excerpt: Months after Elon Musk claimed xAI's AI-generated adaptation of Homer's The Odyssey would outclass Christopher Nolan's film, Grok itself admits the result is 'not historically accurate.'

items.title: Art Spiegelman used AI for sticker on IN THE SHADOW OF NO TOWERS
items.excerpt: Art Spiegelman used AI, with Françoise Mouly writing prompts, to make the cover sticker for a 25th-anniversary edition of In the Shadow of No Towers, saying he wanted an old-engraving look and 'was lazy.'

items.title: Korea Holds 1st AI Creative Contest for Children to Make Webtoons
items.excerpt: South Korea held its first AI creative contest for children to make webtoons; participants received instruction in AI ethics and how to use generative tools before creating their works.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence is a Horror Story
items.excerpt: A Lit Hub essay traces today's AI anxieties back to early science-fiction prophecies of brains severed from bodies, reading artificial intelligence as a horror story.
